title: Give franchise brokers a controlled sales workflow
description: Map each seller, permitted claims and disclosure handoffs before paying for introductions.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Name the seller, the speaker and the duty
paragraphs: Section 436.1 uses a broad franchise-seller definition: franchisors, relevant employees, representatives and agents, subfranchisors and third-party brokers involved in sales. Section 436.9 addresses prohibited seller conduct. The separate disclosure-timing provision places the FDD delivery obligation on the franchisor. Do not compress those different actors into “the broker handles compliance.”

sections.heading: Control the actual sales channels
paragraphs: A referral agreement is only one part of the record. Review presentations, broker portals, webinars, private messages and conversations about likely sales or profit. Sellers must not contradict required disclosures or misrepresent a reference as independent. Financial-performance claims require the rule’s basis, substantiation and disclosure conditions.
bullets: Record each speaker, contracting entity, channel, compensation and permitted territory.
Give the broker approved materials and a named escalation contact for earnings questions.
Keep a versioned record of what was said and which FDD was delivered, with actual dates.

sections.heading: Fictional example: a cleaning-brand introduction
paragraphs: A broker calls a proposed partner a “territory investor” and says a local manager can deliver a predictable margin. Calling the meeting an introduction does not remove a sales claim. The expansion lead should preserve the exact statement, stop its reuse pending review, compare it with Item 19 and route the corrected material through the disclosure owner. This example establishes a review task, not that a particular sale violated the rule.

sections.heading: Output and unresolved gates
paragraphs: Build a seller-responsibility sheet showing who approves materials, supplies the current FDD, records delivery, answers claims questions and checks the relevant states. No offer should rely on the sheet as state sales authorization.

practicalOutput: A seller map, controlled claim library and documented disclosure handoff.
limitations: Federal seller definition and prohibited conduct only; state broker/licensing and sales-authorization requirements are not researched here.

title: Review franchise advertising against the actual disclosure record
description: Separate an ordinary brand message from a performance claim and preserve the exact version used.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: The wording and context matter
paragraphs: The relevant record is the advertisement that a prospective partner actually sees. Federal seller prohibitions apply to oral, visual and written representations. A disclaimer or broker label does not cure a contradiction with required disclosures. An earnings or sales number must be checked against the financial-performance rules and the actual Item 19, rather than justified by a promising home-market result.

sections.heading: Use a short claim register
paragraphs: List each quantitative or implied performance claim, the corresponding disclosed statement, the population and period used, and the written support. Preserve the image, caption, landing page and spoken presentation together.
bullets: Record gross revenue versus profit, included and excluded units, geography and operating model.
Identify testimonials, reference incentives and any asserted independence.
When a source number changes, locate every live version rather than editing one presentation only.

sections.heading: Fictional example: a home-market margin slide
paragraphs: A technical-services brand has one home-country unit with a 20% operating margin and puts “target 20%” in a U.S. recruitment deck. Renaming an achieved number a target does not answer whether the context makes it a performance representation or whether there is a reasonable basis for the U.S. claim. Finance must identify comparability gaps and the disclosure lead must decide whether the slide can be used. This is a fictional review example, not an approved claim.

sections.heading: Keep a release decision
paragraphs: For each version, record approved, revise or pause, the person responsible and the unresolved evidence. Recheck independent state advertising and sales requirements before releasing the campaign. Reading this guide is not campaign approval.

practicalOutput: A versioned advertising-claim register with substantiation and an accountable release decision.
limitations: Does not decide a particular advertisement or authorize state sales. Current state advertising filing and legend rules remain open.

title: Check customer-provision promises against the Business Opportunity Rule
description: An established seller still needs to examine the purchaser’s new business and the promises being sold.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Ask whose business is new
paragraphs: Part 437’s new-business question concerns the prospective purchaser. A seller that has operated for many years cannot dismiss the rule merely because its own business is established. The definition also requires a payment and specified representations that the seller or a designated person will provide locations, accounts/customers or buy back what the purchaser produces.

sections.heading: Distinguish customer supply from ordinary advice
paragraphs: The definition can reach recommended lead-generation or locator services, customer lists and some payment-collection arrangements. General business-development advice, training and advertising alone are not treated as providing customers under that definition. Capture the exact promise and actual arrangement rather than treating every marketing service alike.

sections.heading: A separate disclosure clock, with an unresolved intersection
paragraphs: For an arrangement within Part 437, §437.2 requires the prescribed written disclosure and applicable earnings information at least seven calendar days before the earlier binding agreement or payment/other consideration. Section 437.7 separately requires specified disclosure versions, receipts, contracts and earnings support to be retained for three years.

Important source conflict: the current text of §437.8 uses a $500 figure while cross-referencing the minimum-payment franchise exemption in §436.8(a)(1), whose current threshold is different. This guide does not resolve that interaction, update one text by assumption or conclude an exemption applies. Record it as an unresolved scope gate.

sections.heading: Fictional example and output
paragraphs: A facilities brand sells an established local operator a new cleaning line, required software and a promise of named customer accounts. The fact that both companies already exist does not alone answer the new-line/new-business question. Prepare a factsheet with the purchaser’s activity, payment schedule, exact accounts promise, classification review and applicable disclosure clock before accepting money.

practicalOutput: A Part437 scope factsheet, promise inventory and unresolved franchise-exemption question.
limitations: The literal $500/§436.8(a)(1) cross-reference interaction is unresolved; no exemption conclusion is provided.
State business-opportunity and franchise laws require independent review.

title: Separate company formation from permission to do business in another state
description: Create a state-activity register before assuming one incorporation filing covers the operating footprint.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: “Foreign” can mean another U.S. state
paragraphs: For qualification purposes, an entity formed in one U.S. state can be foreign in another. This is a different use of the word from the owner’s citizenship or an overseas parent. SBA describes possible certificates of authority and, in many states, evidence of good standing. It directs businesses to the individual state offices for requirements and fees.

sections.heading: Map activities before choosing a filing answer
paragraphs: For each entity, record employees and their work locations, premises, customer service, contract performance and intended state expansion. Ask the relevant state office or adviser to apply the actual statutory test. A national website, a single customer or an owner’s address should not be converted into a universal qualification rule here.
bullets: Keep formation, qualification, tax accounts and sector permits in separate columns.
Record the legal entity that employs staff and signs each local contract.
Assign annual-report and registered-agent responsibilities where applicable.

sections.heading: Fictional example: formation in Delaware, operations elsewhere
paragraphs: A Singapore-owned company forms a Delaware LLC but proposes a staffed service depot in Texas. Delaware formation is evidence of entity creation; it does not answer Texas qualification, payroll tax, customer-site licences or the depot’s occupancy conditions. The practical next step is a Texas activity dossier and a dated requirement check, not a second unsupported incorporation recommendation.

sections.heading: Output
paragraphs: Create one register per operating entity, with formation documents, each additional-state activity, the authority consulted, filing decision, evidence and recurring owner. Keep unresolved qualification explicitly unresolved.

practicalOutput: An entity-by-state activity and qualification register with separate tax and permit workstreams.
limitations: SBA overview only; no individual state threshold, exemption, filing fee or tax-nexus determination was researched.

title: An LLC’s legal form does not settle its federal tax classification
description: Prepare the ownership, default classification and election dates before filing Form 8832.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Separate three questions
paragraphs: State-law entity form, federal tax classification and the owner’s immigration position answer different questions. A domestic eligible entity with two or more members generally defaults to partnership classification; a single-owner eligible entity generally defaults to disregarded status unless an election applies. The foreign-entity defaults differ and depend in part on limited liability. Do not copy the domestic default onto the overseas parent.

sections.heading: An election has a dated procedure
paragraphs: Section 301.7701-3 and the Form 8832 instructions govern eligible-entity elections. The ordinary effective-date window is up to 75 days before filing and up to 12 months after filing. A change election generally has a 60-month restriction, with exceptions; an initial election effective on formation is treated differently. Late relief has conditions and is not assumed. The retrieved form is revision December 2013, not a newly issued 2026 form.

sections.heading: Fictional example: a wholly foreign-owned LLC
paragraphs: An overseas company forms a one-member domestic LLC and assumes “disregarded” means no U.S. information return. Classification alone does not answer Form 5472 and related pro-forma return obligations for reportable transactions. The CFO should record the owner, entity, transactions and proposed election before obtaining a filing conclusion. This example does not recommend a tax structure or assert a specific return is due.

sections.heading: Output and responsibilities
paragraphs: Prepare an entity-classification brief with the exact legal entity, jurisdiction, owners, liability characteristics, default, intended treatment, effective date, EIN and returns affected. Finance owns the dates; a tax reviewer decides the applicable election and reporting position.

practicalOutput: An entity-classification and election-date brief, linked to separate foreign-owned reporting tasks.
limitations: Not a recommendation to form an LLC or elect corporate/partnership treatment. No tax savings, treaty or immigration result is promised.

title: Build evidence for royalties and services between related companies
description: A percentage copied from a partner contract is not a transfer-pricing method.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Identify the controlled transactions
paragraphs: A foreign parent may license a brand, provide remote support, lend working capital and supply products to its U.S. affiliate. Those are distinct transactions with different facts. Section 1.482-1 asks whether the results are consistent with dealings between uncontrolled taxpayers in comparable circumstances. “Our standard royalty is 6%” is not itself evidence that the controlled arrangement is arm’s length.

sections.heading: Prepare facts before choosing a method
paragraphs: The best-method rule seeks the most reliable measure under the facts and circumstances; it does not provide a universal first-choice percentage. Reliability depends on comparability, data quality and assumptions. Services and intangibles have additional method provisions outside this scoped review.
bullets: Document who develops, owns, funds and maintains the IP.
List actual support deliverables, staff time, costs and who benefits.
Identify operating functions, assets and risks in each entity.
Keep third-party comparables separate from internal policy rates and explain material differences.

sections.heading: Fictional example: a service bundle
paragraphs: A European parent invoices its new U.S. subsidiary one royalty covering brand use, training and quarterly technical support. A useful first output separates the rights and services, shows the staff and costs, and records the U.S. entity’s actual functions. It does not assume every cost is chargeable, that all services are one transaction, or that a franchisee’s unrelated-party rate can be copied without adjustment.

sections.heading: Give finance an evidence ledger
paragraphs: Record the agreement, actual conduct, method question, data source, allocation assumptions, invoice and payment currency. Transfer-pricing support and withholding compliance are separate workstreams; neither is established by a well-written intercompany contract alone.

practicalOutput: A controlled-transaction evidence ledger and specific method/comparability questions for tax review.
limitations: Review limited to §1.482-1(a)–(c); transaction-specific methods, documentation rules, treaties and foreign-country transfer pricing are not comprehensively researched.

title: Separate a U.S. business visit from doing the operating work
description: Turn a proposed founder trip into an activity schedule instead of inferring work permission from company ownership.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: The activity is the starting point
paragraphs: An owner can remain abroad and still plan meetings with a proposed U.S. partner. The State Department lists consulting with business associates, attending relevant conferences and negotiating contracts among B-1 business examples. It separately lists employment as prohibited on visitor visas. Owning a U.S. company or receiving payment overseas does not by itself settle which side a planned activity falls on.

sections.heading: Describe the trip precisely
paragraphs: Write what happens each day, who receives the benefit, who performs the work and how the traveller is paid. “Launch support” is too vague when it might mean investor meetings, interviewing a manager, training staff or servicing a customer. These activities should not be treated as interchangeable.
bullets: Separate negotiation and observation from hands-on delivery or ordinary management work.
Identify the host, customer sites, proposed duration and repeat-visit pattern.
Keep the evidence and unresolved activity question with the trip owner.

sections.heading: Fictional example: the technical founder
paragraphs: A founder proposes three days negotiating a distribution contract followed by two weeks repairing customer equipment alongside the new team. The meeting examples do not establish permission for the repair work. Split the itinerary and obtain an activity-specific answer before booking the operational portion. This guide does not decide that a particular alternative visa is available.

sections.heading: Output
paragraphs: Produce a visit-activity brief with permitted-purpose evidence and unresolved tasks. A visa does not guarantee admission; the admitting authorities decide entry. Keep any L-1, E-2 or other work-authorised staffing plan as its own workstream.

practicalOutput: A dated trip-activity brief separating meetings from unresolved operational work.
limitations: No individual visa, ESTA, admission, productive-training or hands-on service conclusion is provided.

title: Budget a hired manager and team using the federal workweek rules
description: Check coverage and nonexempt hours before converting a home-market labour percentage into a U.S. plan.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Do not use $500,000 as a universal escape
paragraphs: DOL Fact Sheet 14 distinguishes enterprise coverage from individual coverage. The ordinary enterprise test includes at least two employees and at least $500,000 in annual business volume, while specified institutions have different coverage treatment. Individual interstate-commerce coverage can apply even if the enterprise does not meet that volume. A small launch budget is not a no-wage-law conclusion.

sections.heading: Use the workweek, not a monthly average
paragraphs: Fact Sheet 23 explains overtime for covered nonexempt employees after 40 hours in a fixed 168-hour workweek. Averaging a busy week with a quiet week is not permitted. Paying a salary does not itself remove overtime rights, and an advance-approval policy does not waive overtime already earned. This guide does not quote a current salary-exemption threshold or determine who qualifies for an exemption.

sections.heading: Fictional worked example: 45 hours
paragraphs: Assume a covered, nonexempt technician works 45 hours at a $20 regular hourly rate, with no other compensation affecting that rate. Straight-time pay is 45 × $20 = $900; the additional overtime premium is 5 × $10 = $50, for $950 total before employer burden. This is fictional arithmetic, not a local wage quotation or a complete regular-rate calculation. A second week of 35 hours does not erase the first week’s overtime.

sections.heading: Build the staffing evidence
paragraphs: Record the employer, actual duties, reporting lines, weekly schedule, all compensation components and timekeeping owner. Add separate state/local wage, leave and tax-account tasks. Keep an exemption or worker-status question unresolved until the relevant facts and current rules have been checked.

practicalOutput: A weekly staffing-cost worksheet with coverage, duties, regular-rate and local-law questions.
limitations: No current executive/administrative/professional salary threshold, independent-contractor or joint-employer conclusion.
Federal fact sheets are scoped guidance; current state/local obligations and all compensation components require separate review.

title: Assign safety responsibilities before the first customer-site job
description: Separate the employer’s legal duties from brand support and customer procurement conditions.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Start with the job and the employer
paragraphs: Section 5 sets the employer’s general duty and duty to comply with applicable standards. A partner-operated cleaning or maintenance business needs an actual safety system for its work, not simply a clause saying “the operator handles safety.” Identify who employs and directs each worker and where the work occurs before allocating tasks.

sections.heading: Separate three sources of obligations
paragraphs: Applicable law, a customer’s site rules and the brand’s operating standards can overlap but are different records. The OSHA employer-responsibilities overview covers safe workplaces, applicable standards, hazard information and training. A customer’s insurance certificate or induction card is not evidence that every legal standard has been met.
bullets: List chemicals, equipment, access conditions and foreseeable task hazards.
Identify the relevant federal OSHA or state-plan authority and task-specific standards.
Name who supplies equipment, conducts training, authorises work and responds to incidents.

sections.heading: Fictional example: remote support, local delivery
paragraphs: A foreign facilities brand trains a U.S. partner remotely. The partner’s team will work at a customer site using powered equipment. The practical output is an employer/site/hazard map with missing training and equipment evidence, plus questions about each entity’s actual control. The brand’s remote location does not decide the legal employer analysis, and this guide does not make that determination.

sections.heading: Output
paragraphs: Before the first job, the local operating lead should hold dated training, equipment and site-permission evidence and a clear escalation route. Keep unresearched standards and state-plan differences visible as unresolved tasks.

practicalOutput: An employer/site safety responsibility map and evidence checklist for the first job.
limitations: No task-specific OSHA standard, state-plan rule, incident-reporting deadline or joint-employer determination has been researched here.

title: Give the local employer an I-9 timing and retention owner
description: A foreign owner staying abroad still needs an operational hire-verification workflow in the U.S. business.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Assign the operational role
paragraphs: The entity hiring the employee needs a verification process even when the parent company and owner remain overseas. Section 274a.2(b)(1) sets employee and employer timing. The employee completes Section 1 at hire; the employer generally examines the required evidence and completes Section 2 within three business days of hire. For employment of less than three business days, the employer examination/completion occurs at hire.

sections.heading: Do not improvise a remote procedure
paragraphs: The regulation recognises physical examination or an alternative procedure authorised under its specified provision. That reference does not make every video call, scanned passport or overseas manager review sufficient. Obtain the current official form, acceptable-document instructions and any authorised alternative-procedure conditions before using the process. The USCIS instruction PDF returned HTTP 403 during this review; its current edition and detailed procedure remain unverified here.

sections.heading: Retention depends on both dates
paragraphs: For an employer, §274a.2(b)(2)(i) requires retention for three years after hire or one year after employment ends, whichever is later. In a fictional example, a hire on January 15, 2027 and termination on January 15, 2030 produces a later retention endpoint of January 15, 2031. This illustration is not a live personnel record or a conclusion about another retention duty.

sections.heading: Output and privacy
paragraphs: Create a task register with hire dates, verification owner, completion evidence and retention calculation. Keep identity documents and completed forms in the employer’s controlled personnel system; do not put them in this site’s planning notes. Track any current-form or remote-procedure question as unresolved until the official instructions can be checked.

practicalOutput: A hire-verification calendar and retention worksheet without identity-document uploads.
limitations: Current USCIS form edition and detailed acceptable-document/remote-procedure instructions could not be read because the PDF returned 403.
No individual work-authorisation, anti-discrimination, E-Verify or immigration-category determination.

title: Name the importer of record before shipping branded equipment or stock
description: A freight quote and a delivery term do not replace the legal-party and recordkeeping check.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Separate the commercial and legal roles
paragraphs: For a launch shipment, identify the seller, purchaser, owner, consignee, proposed importer of record, customs broker and ultimate recipient. Section 1484 requires the importer-of-record entry/completion information using reasonable care. Its eligible-filer language includes the owner or purchaser and an appropriately designated licensed person under the stated conditions. A carrier’s or forwarder’s name on a quote does not alone answer those roles.

sections.heading: Collect the entry evidence before dispatch
paragraphs: Section 141.11 addresses evidence of the right to make entry through specified shipping-document arrangements. Link those records with the commercial invoice, actual product description, classification, value, origin and any product-agency requirements. The broker needs accurate underlying facts; outsourcing filing is not a substitute for defining the responsible parties.

sections.heading: Use a category-specific retention schedule
paragraphs: Section 163.4 generally uses five years from entry or the activity that created the record, but lists exceptions, including particular drawback, packing-list, informal consignee and carrier records. Do not set every customs document to “five years” without identifying its category and any other applicable rule.

sections.heading: Fictional example and output
paragraphs: An overseas brand sends demonstration machines to a partner and assumes the partner’s warehouse will handle importation. Before dispatch, operations should obtain the actual importer/broker authority, product and value evidence, intended use and return/disposal plan. A shipment-role sheet should record each document owner and unresolved customs or product requirement. No shipment is cleared by this example.

practicalOutput: A shipment-role and customs-evidence sheet with a category-specific retention owner.
limitations: No product classification, customs value, bond, nonresident-importer eligibility or agency admissibility determination.

title: Build a dated tariff evidence ledger instead of guessing an all-in rate
description: Start with the exact product and legal schedule before putting a duty percentage into unit economics.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: A product name is not a tariff classification
paragraphs: Describe materials, function, composition, dimensions and how the goods are presented at entry. USITC’s HTS help explains the classification framework and access to legal notes and CBP ruling resources. A similar catalogue label can hide a legally significant product difference. Keep a proposed code labelled proposed until the relevant analysis is done.

sections.heading: Keep base and additional duties separate
paragraphs: The schedule contains legal notes and Chapter 99 provisions that may affect the calculation. Record the schedule version/date, candidate classification, country facts, any claimed preference and each additional-duty or exclusion question. This guide does not quote a current rate or conclude which temporary measure applies.

sections.heading: Fictional example: two cleaning machines
paragraphs: A brand plans to ship a powered scrubber and a replacement battery. Treating the combined shipment as “cleaning equipment at 5%” leaves the product distinctions, classification and any additional measures untested. The finance model should show the duty cells as unknown until supported, and test a clearly labelled estimate separately from a verified rate.

sections.heading: Output
paragraphs: Give the customs reviewer a product evidence pack and a dated rate ledger, with the authority, scope, effective date, unresolved issue and person responsible for each entry. Recalculate landed cost when a product, supplier, origin or legal provision changes.

practicalOutput: A product-specific classification and tariff evidence ledger feeding the landed-cost model.
limitations: Workflow only: no current tariff rate, temporary measure, exclusion, product code or origin preference has been substantively verified.

title: Separate origin marking from tariff and brand nationality
description: Trace manufacturing steps before labelling an imported product with the headquarters country.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Which origin question are you answering?
paragraphs: Brand ownership, shipping point, country-of-origin marking and preferential tariff origin are distinct questions. For the marking part, §134.1(b) starts with manufacture, production or growth and addresses further work that effects substantial transformation. It expressly points to part 102 for the relevant NAFTA/USMCA-country marking cases. Do not replace that framework with “our company is incorporated in Singapore.”

sections.heading: Use the general marking rule with its limits
paragraphs: Section 134.11 states that foreign-origin articles, or their containers as applicable, generally need a conspicuous, legible, indelible and sufficiently permanent English country name indicating origin to the ultimate U.S. purchaser. The part contains exceptions and special rules. A general quotation does not settle whether this product, container or downstream processing qualifies for an exception.

sections.heading: Fictional example: assembly in a second country
paragraphs: A European brand buys components in one country and assembles its equipment in another before shipment to the United States. A “European brand” sticker does not establish the manufacturing-origin answer. Operations should document each process, materials and product state before/after assembly, then obtain a product-specific marking analysis. This guide makes no substantial-transformation finding.

sections.heading: Output
paragraphs: Keep a manufacturing-origin map, proposed artwork and evidence question for each product. Link the marking conclusion to the tariff ledger without assuming they apply the same test. Recheck when the supplier or production steps change.

practicalOutput: A manufacturing-origin map and proposed-marking review pack, separate from tariff preference.
limitations: No product-specific origin determination, marking exception, part102 analysis, preferential eligibility or trade-remedy result.

title: Identify the food FSVP importer before the first shipment
description: The customs broker, FDA registration contact and FSVP importer are not interchangeable roles.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Name the legally defined importer
paragraphs: Under §1.500, the FSVP importer is the U.S. owner or consignee of the food offered for import. If none exists at entry, it is a U.S. agent or representative of the foreign owner or consignee, with the required signed consent. The roles can differ from the customs importer, freight forwarder or foreign facility registration contact; map them rather than assuming one broker performs all of them.

sections.heading: A supplier certificate is not the whole program
paragraphs: Section 1.502 generally requires a program for each imported food, subject to the rule’s scope. FDA’s overview describes qualified individuals, hazard analysis, supplier evaluation, appropriate verification, corrective action and reevaluation. The required verification depends on the food and supplier; do not assume every case needs the same audit or that a certificate automatically suffices. Keep the practical matrix at food-and-foreign-supplier level so a changed supplier is visible for reassessment; this is not a claim that a separate physical document is always required.

sections.heading: Check scope and the entry data
paragraphs: Part 1 contains exemptions and modified requirements, including specified USDA-regulated meat, poultry and egg products. “Exempt from FSVP” does not mean unrestricted food importation. Section 1.509 requires importer name, email and an FDA-acceptable unique facility identifier at each line entry and, where relevant, designation before import. Exact category, labelling, prior notice, facility registration and other admissibility duties remain separate questions.

sections.heading: Fictional example and output
paragraphs: A training brand sends a branded packaged snack to its U.S. partner for resale. Before shipment, the supply lead must identify the food and supplier, actual U.S. purchaser at entry, FSVP owner, program evidence and separate food requirements. No “small sample” or “small business” exemption is assumed. Produce a food/party/program matrix with unresolved category questions.

practicalOutput: A food-specific FSVP role and program evidence matrix before shipment.
limitations: No complete food-category, hazard, small-importer, dietary-supplement, labelling, prior-notice, facility-registration or USDA import analysis.

title: Search U.S. trademark rights beyond an exact federal name match
description: Give the brand owner a dated clearance evidence pack before a partner invests in signs or software.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: An exact federal match is only one search
paragraphs: USPTO explains that a comprehensive search looks for confusingly similar marks for the same or related goods and services. Spelling, sound, appearance and meaning can matter. Federal registered and pending records are important, but state records and common-law use can also matter. A clean exact-name result is not a conclusion that the name is available.

sections.heading: Scope the search to the real U.S. offer
paragraphs: List the word mark, logo, abbreviations, translations and proposed goods/services. Search relevant related services and channels, not only the brand’s current home-country category. Preserve result identifiers, status, owner, apparent use and the date checked.
bullets: Separate registered/pending records from observed marketplace use.
Record similar names and related services, even where the spelling differs.
Keep gaps, uncertain use dates and geographic limitations visible.

sections.heading: Fictional example: facilities brand enters software
paragraphs: A facilities-services brand plans to license both its name and a scheduling app in the United States. A home-market registration and an exact federal search in cleaning services do not settle related software/service conflicts. The practical output is a search pack covering the actual offer, with competing uses and questions assigned for review before signage and app rollout.

sections.heading: Output
paragraphs: The brand owner should retain a dated clearance brief, the search scope, results and unresolved risks. A partner’s contract acknowledgement is not a substitute for investigating the rights being licensed. Registration strategy, ownership chain and quality-control terms remain separate tasks.

practicalOutput: A dated U.S. mark-search brief covering variants, related services and non-federal use.
limitations: No legal clearance, likelihood-of-confusion finding, registration guarantee, ownership-chain audit or licence quality-control determination.

title: Transfer operating know-how with evidence of secrecy and lawful access
description: An NDA alone does not establish that every manual page is a protected trade secret.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Identify the information and the measures
paragraphs: Section 1839 does not treat everything called confidential as a trade secret. The owner needs reasonable measures to keep the information secret and independent economic value from it not being generally known or readily ascertainable by proper means. Document the actual know-how, access limits, distribution and reasons for value; do not label public marketing material a secret by assertion.

sections.heading: Make lawful use and exit practical
paragraphs: Map which partner employees need which material, where it is stored, how accounts are issued and revoked, and which copies can be retained. The statute’s definitions distinguish misappropriation from lawful independent development and reverse engineering. A broad contractual label does not establish the statutory facts or prohibit protected reporting.

sections.heading: Preserve the whistleblower notice distinction
paragraphs: Section 1833(b) protects specified confidential disclosures to government officials or an attorney solely to report/investigate suspected legal violations, and sealed court filings under its conditions. Covered employer agreements governing trade secrets/confidential information need the immunity notice or qualifying policy cross-reference. The covered employee definition includes individual contractors and consultants. The notice rule applies to agreements entered into or updated after May 11, 2016. Missing notice limits the specified exemplary-damages and attorney-fee remedies against the affected employee; it does not automatically void every contract or remove every remedy.

sections.heading: Fictional example and output
paragraphs: A training business gives a U.S. manager unrestricted access to manuals, pricing files and customer data. Before transfer, the operations lead should separate public material, claimed secrets and personal data, apply proportionate access controls and check recipient agreements and the covered notice. Produce a know-how/access/exit register. Cross-border personal-data law is a separate unresolved workstream, not satisfied by trade-secret controls.

practicalOutput: A know-how classification, access and exit register with a covered-agreement notice check.
limitations: No finding that specific information is a trade secret or that a particular contract is covered; state law, remedies and cross-border privacy remain separate.

title: An L-1 staff plan needs a qualifying job and employment history
description: Move beyond the corporate ownership diagram to the person, actual role and new-office evidence.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: The company relationship is only one gate
paragraphs: The regulation distinguishes the qualifying corporate relationship from the worker’s history and proposed duties. It generally calls for one continuous year of qualifying full-time employment abroad within the relevant preceding three-year period and evidence of the actual executive, managerial or specialised-knowledge capacity. An impressive title, licence agreement or long relationship with a supplier does not supply those facts.

sections.heading: Describe what the person will actually do
paragraphs: The managerial definition addresses organisational/function management, appropriate authority and discretion; a first-line supervisor is not a manager solely because of supervision, subject to the professional-employee qualification. Executive and specialised-knowledge definitions have their own elements. Build a task/time and reporting-line record instead of copying “general manager” onto every job. Brief lawful U.S. trips can have specific treatment in the continuous-employment calculation; do not count them automatically as foreign employment.

sections.heading: A new office needs its own evidence
paragraphs: For a new-office manager/executive, the regulation requires sufficient physical premises and evidence that the intended operation will support the qualifying position within one year of approval, including the proposed organisation and financial ability. The specialised-knowledge new-office provisions differ. An owner or major stockholder also has specified temporary-service/assignment-abroad evidence under subsection (l)(3)(vii). These are regulatory evidence categories, not a generic minimum-investment promise.

sections.heading: Practical output
paragraphs: Create a person-by-role matrix with foreign employment dates, travel, duties, authority, supporting staff, evidence custodian and unresolved questions. Link it to the corporate relationship diagram but keep each gate separate. The owner can remain abroad while a properly assessed team carries out the U.S. roles; no founder relocation or individual approval is assumed.

practicalOutput: A person/role/employment/new-office evidence matrix linked to the existing entity relationship map.
limitations: Scoped 8 CFR review; no current form edition, fee, processing time, role qualification, petition approval or admission conclusion.

title: A service business cannot borrow a blanket P.L. 86-272 exemption
description: Separate tax types and actual activities before treating out-of-state incorporation as protection.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Read what the federal protection actually covers
paragraphs: Section 381 addresses a state or political subdivision’s net income tax where the person’s only in-state activities are the specified solicitation of orders for tangible personal property, with out-of-state approval/rejection and fulfilment conditions. It does not say that every out-of-state company, website, royalty recipient or service provider is exempt from state taxes.

sections.heading: Keep tax types separate
paragraphs: A service business should not apply a tangible-goods solicitation rule to cleaning, consulting, training or managed IT income by analogy. Nor does a net-income-tax limit settle sales/use tax, payroll withholding, unemployment tax, gross-receipts tax or corporate qualification. The statute also excludes specified state-incorporated corporations and resident/domiciled individuals from that protection. No positive nexus result for a particular state is determined by this guide.

sections.heading: Prepare the facts that a state analysis needs
paragraphs: For each legal entity and state, record employees/contractors and work locations, customer performance, premises, products, contracts, solicitation, approval and fulfilment. Identify the tax type before asking for a threshold. Section 381’s defined independent-contractor treatment is not a general employment-status ruling.
bullets: Use separate rows for income/franchise, sales/use, payroll and local taxes.
Record the authority, source date and unresolved trigger instead of writing “no physical office, no tax.”
Keep formation/qualification evidence separate from the tax decision.

sections.heading: Output
paragraphs: Produce a state-by-tax activity register with an explicit “P.L. 86-272 relevance” question only where its actual goods/activity conditions may matter. A transaction-specific state analysis still needs the current state rules; no 50-state clearance is supplied.

practicalOutput: A state-by-tax activity register that prevents an unsupported tangible-goods exemption being applied to services.
limitations: Federal statutory boundary only; current individual state/local nexus, economic thresholds, taxability, sourcing, apportionment and returns remain unresearched.

title: Texas service taxability depends on the task, not the “IT” label
description: Use the official data-processing/professional-service distinction to build a service-line evidence schedule.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Describe the delivered service
paragraphs: The Comptroller describes entering, storing, manipulating or retrieving a customer’s data as data processing, while merely using a computer to perform a professional service is different. Its examples contrast data work with engineering/bookkeeping judgement and interpretation. A business’s “IT”, “consulting” or “B2B” label does not establish every invoice line’s taxability.

sections.heading: Mixed work needs evidence, not relabelling
paragraphs: The publication addresses distinct/identifiable nontaxable services, reasonable separate charges and documentation where taxable and nontaxable work are bundled. It also describes allocation where a customer uses services inside and outside Texas. A contract line renamed “consulting” is not a substitute for the actual deliverables and use facts.

The Legislature’s recovered current full text now supplies the statutory check: § 151.0035 defines data processing and exclusions; § 151.0101(a)(12) lists data processing as a taxable service; and § 151.351 exempts 20 percent of the value of information services and data processing services. This is a partial exemption of qualifying service value, not a 20% tax rate or a blanket exemption for every IT contract.

Arithmetic illustration: if $1,000 is otherwise-taxable qualifying data-processing service value, the § 151.351 exemption is $200 and the remaining value is $800 before any other applicable adjustments. The actual tax amount still depends on applicable rates, nexus, sourcing, customer use and other facts; this example is not a quote or a determination of a contract’s treatment.

sections.heading: Practical service-line exercise
paragraphs: Take one actual proposed contract and list each deliverable: data entry, hosting/storage, interpreting results, advisory work and any separate product. For each, record the customer’s data, staff judgement, location/use, price evidence and unresolved category. Do not upload the confidential contract here; retain it with the finance custodian.
bullets: Separate service classification from seller nexus/registration.
Check exemptions and the taxable base before computing a tax amount.
Keep customer multistate-use certificates and allocation evidence in the authorised accounting process.

sections.heading: Output
paragraphs: Prepare a service-line taxability evidence schedule for the Texas activity, with unknown treatment clearly marked. A final state-specific answer needs the current authority and actual facts; other states, including Washington’s separately amended service categories, are not determined by this Texas example.

practicalOutput: A Texas service-line classification, billing and use-allocation evidence schedule.
limitations: Current statutory review is scoped to Texas Tax Code §§ 151.0035,151.0101 and 151.351, with Comptroller guidance revision 03/2022. Actual classification, mixed-service allocation, exemptions, nexus, sourcing and applicable tax amounts remain fact-specific.
No final tax percentage, Texas permit/nexus/sourcing determination or other-state taxability conclusion.

title: A UK company address does not establish U.S.–UK treaty benefits
description: Build separate residence, income, beneficial-owner and limitation-on-benefits evidence.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Four questions, four evidence sets
paragraphs: The payee’s incorporation/address, its treaty residence, beneficial ownership of the income and eligibility under an applicable limitation-on-benefits provision are distinct questions. IRS guidance expressly lists these conditions for treaty withholding claims. A form or treaty-country mailing address is not a substitute for the underlying entitlement; the payer must consider actual knowledge or reason to know of ineligibility.

sections.heading: Use the actual UK treaty and its amendment
paragraphs: Article 4 defines residence with its own scope. Article 12 addresses royalties and also includes permanent-establishment, special-relationship and conduit conditions. Article 23 contains multiple eligibility routes and limitations. For example, the ownership/base-erosion route in Article 23(2)(f) has both ownership-period and deductible-payment conditions, not simply a UK incorporation test. The July 2002 protocol replaces Article 23(7)(d); do not rely on the unamended equivalent-beneficiary wording in the 2001 PDF. This guide does not decide a post-Brexit or derivative-benefit question.

sections.heading: Prepare a claim dossier, not a rate assumption
paragraphs: Finance should identify the actual rights/payment, payee, tax treatment, owners and relevant period, deductible outflows, business activity and proposed LOB route. Record which paragraph is being relied on and the missing evidence. Do not copy one qualifying-person path onto a different entity or another country’s treaty.
bullets: Keep residence and beneficial-owner evidence separate from the E-2 nationality map.
Link any withholding certificate to the actual recipient/income and dated entitlement evidence.
Recheck changes of ownership, payee, arrangement or treaty conditions.

sections.heading: Output
paragraphs: Create an article-by-article evidence schedule with each condition, custodian, source, period and unresolved issue. Keep the cash model’s treaty assumption unknown until supported. This supplements the general foreign-royalty payment guide with a specific treaty/LOB work product; it is not a tax eligibility conclusion.

practicalOutput: A U.S.–UK treaty claim evidence dossier covering residence, income, beneficial owner and LOB conditions.
limitations: U.S.–UK illustration only; no withholding rate, treaty entitlement, permanent-establishment, conduit, equivalent-beneficiary or post-Brexit determination.

title: Plan trademark quality controls separately from franchise classification
description: Map what the licence protects before treating every operating requirement as the same legal control.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: The statutes address marked goods and services
paragraphs: Section 1127’s related-company definition turns on the mark owner’s control over the nature and quality of the goods or services. Section 1055 describes legitimate related-company use and controlled first use inuring to the registrant/applicant, with its public-deception condition. These provisions are a reason to identify the actual quality system, not a warrant to impose or abandon any particular operational rule.

sections.heading: Use a control-purpose matrix
paragraphs: For each proposed standard, record what quality attribute it protects, how it is checked, who acts on a defect and whether it also directs the method of running the business. The FTC classification framework asks its own brand, significant-control/assistance and payment questions. A contract heading “trademark protection” does not decide those facts.
bullets: Separate logo/artwork approval from scheduling, staffing, sales methods and mandatory systems.
Describe the actual product/service outcome and inspection/correction process.
Record which controls have mixed purposes rather than forcing a false single label.

sections.heading: Keep the two review outputs visible
paragraphs: One output is the mark-use/quality evidence: owner, authorised user, standards, inspection and corrections. The second is the broader operating relationship factsheet for federal and independent state analysis. Removing all oversight to avoid one legal test can create a different unanswered trademark question; adding detailed business controls can create classification questions. No particular contract is declared valid or a franchise by this guide.

sections.heading: Output
paragraphs: Prepare a control-purpose matrix and route each unresolved issue to the relevant workstream. The exact licence, actual conduct and applicable cases must be reviewed before making an abandonment, validity or coverage conclusion. This is a statutory distinction, not a complete naked-licensing doctrine survey.

practicalOutput: A mark-quality versus business-operation control-purpose matrix with separate evidence and questions.
limitations: Statutory distinction only; no complete trademark case-law, licence-validity, abandonment or franchise-coverage determination.

title: A name search is one part of sanctions and export diligence
description: Keep identity, blocked ownership and transaction restrictions separate before relying on a partner-screening result.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Resolve identity before interpreting a result
paragraphs: The Consolidated Screening List combines multiple Commerce, State and Treasury lists as an aid. Commerce says an apparent match needs additional due diligence and official source confirmation before action. A fuzzy-name score measures similarity, not the probability that a deal is lawful. Record aliases, identifiers, addresses, source list and search date, including why an apparent match is or is not the same party.

sections.heading: Unlisted ownership can still matter
paragraphs: OFAC FAQ 401 explains direct/indirect ownership and aggregation under the 50 Percent Rule. Its own examples show why multiplying percentages mechanically can mislead: a blocked person owning 50% of Entity A makes A blocked, and A’s 50% ownership of Entity B can make B blocked. Record the chain and applicable rule instead of treating “not named” as “not blocked.”

sections.heading: Below50% is not a universal permission
paragraphs: FAQ 398 says control without 50%-aggregate ownership is not automatic blocking under this ownership rule, but warns about other designation/blocking criteria and dealings with a blocked representative. Party screening also does not decide product/technology, destination, end-use, country-programme or authorisation restrictions. Do not treat all OFAC listings as identical, or every country connection as a blanket ban.

sections.heading: Output
paragraphs: Prepare a screening-and-transaction evidence register with identity resolution, ownership, source-specific restriction, transaction facts, unresolved questions and a person responsible before payment/access/shipment. Repeat the check when relevant parties, ownership, goods or restrictions change. This site does not perform live screening or issue a clean-partner certification.

practicalOutput: A party/ownership/transaction screening register with source-specific restrictions and unresolved authorisation questions.
limitations: No live name search, current designation result, country/programme, export classification, licence or transaction clearance.

title: Separate price policy, vertical restraints and competitor coordination
description: A federal rule-of-reason standard is a review framework, not blanket permission for a network price rule.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Use the actual documented holding
paragraphs: In Leegin Creative Leather Products v. PSKS, 551 U.S. 877 (2007), the Supreme Court majority overruled the prior Dr. Miles federal per-se approach to vertical minimum resale-price agreements and required rule-of-reason analysis. It reversed and remanded; that procedural result is not a finding that every policy or the particular arrangement was lawful. The complete official U.S. Reports decision is available from the Library of Congress, and current FTC guidance explains the federal/state distinction.

sections.heading: A brand network can contain several relationships
paragraphs: FTC guidance discusses manufacturer/dealer restrictions, unilateral policy decisions and competitor coordination. Map who actually competes, who supplies whom and whether dealers/operators coordinate or pressure the brand collectively. Calling a contract vertical is not a legal result, especially when the brand also competes at another level or the arrangement has horizontal effects.

sections.heading: Preserve the actual policy and commercial purpose
paragraphs: Record suggested versus required prices, resale/customer-service prices, discounts, advertising support, territories, reserved customers and how compliance is induced. Keep dealer communications and the claimed service/quality investment evidence. State and international minimum-price treatment can differ from the federal framework. MAP and MFN conditions also need their own actual scope; one headline rule does not clear all of them.

sections.heading: Output
paragraphs: Build a policy/party/effects evidence pack with a source-specific federal/state question for each restriction. The legal standard guides what must be examined; it is not a badge of legality. Use this before announcing a standard network price or agreeing an allocation with other operators.

practicalOutput: A pricing/territory-policy evidence pack with party relationships, communications, effects and separate state questions.
limitations: No antitrust clearance or later Leegin merits outcome; source review uses the 2007 majority’s standard/disposition plus current FTC guidance, not a full jurisdiction/case-law survey.

title: Separate the contractor rule, enforcement policy and tax test
description: Prepare actual worker facts without treating a label, a proposed rule or an agency enforcement choice as one universal test.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Use a status table before a factor checklist
paragraphs: As reviewed on November 12, 2026, the current eCFR Part 795 still displays the 2024 economic-reality interpretation. It uses the whole activity and six nonexclusive factors; no single factor or subset is necessarily dispositive. The May 1, 2025 WHD bulletin tells investigators not to apply that analysis in its stated scope and expressly says it does not change employees’ rights or employers’ responsibilities. Those are different source types.

rows: That agency policy replaces governing court law
Investigation policy using 2008 Fact Sheet 13, subject to scope/discretion
A repeal, private-right waiver or closed-case reopening
Proposed rescission/replacement and proposed expansion to FMLA/MSPA
An effective replacement simply because comments closed

sections.heading: Collect facts that survive a change of framework
paragraphs: Record who sets prices/schedules, accepts jobs, hires helpers, buys entrepreneurial assets, markets to others and bears a genuine opportunity for profit or loss. Record actual practice as well as reserved rights. Under the codified interpretation, specialised skill alone does not establish an independent business, and a licence, contract label or remote work location does not settle the status. Do not turn the factors into a point score.

sections.heading: Keep federal employment tax and state tests separate
paragraphs: IRS guidance groups common-law evidence into behavioural control, financial control and the type of relationship. It requires the whole relationship, not a magic number of factors; the right to control can matter for remote workers. A payroll-tax determination or relief provision is not a universal FLSA or state unemployment answer. Give each actual jurisdiction/test its own source and unresolved task.

sections.heading: What the actual litigation record establishes
paragraphs: In its January 9, 2025 Colt & Joe Trucking opinion/order, the New Mexico district court found that the challenger lacked standing and explained that its arguments would otherwise fail or were waived. That is a procedural outcome in a rule challenge, not a classification of every driver or service technician. The February 2026 NPRM reports appeals/stays in this and other challenges as of that publication; this guide does not claim an independently checked current appellate docket or an unqualified nationwide merits outcome.

sections.heading: Output
paragraphs: Prepare one worker-facts dossier and a separate test/status register with source, date, actor, missing evidence and responsible person. Keep the proposed 2026 analysis labelled proposed and obtain the governing current court/state answer for the actual arrangement before relying on contractor treatment.

practicalOutput: A worker-facts dossier and dated rule/policy/proposal/court/tax test register.
limitations: No individual worker, state-law, exemption or tax-relief conclusion.
Latest appellate docket/status is not independently verified; the 2026 NPRM’s case account is dated historical agency reporting.
FAB and NPRM cite different associated opinion numbers; this guide does not reconcile or apply those opinions.

title: A brand control clause does not answer every joint-employer test
description: Separate the current NLRA text from FLSA duties, proposed changes and actual employment conduct.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: The current NLRA rule was actually restored
paragraphs: The NLRB’s February 27, 2026 final action says the 2023 rule never took effect after district-court vacatur and restores the 2020 text immediately. Current § 103.40 matches that action: substantial direct and immediate control over one or more listed essential employment terms is central; indirect or unexercised reserved authority has the rule’s qualified supplementary role. This is the NLRA inquiry, not a rule for every employment statute.

sections.heading: Read the documented court step accurately
paragraphs: The Chamber of Commerce v. NLRB opinion/order was ordered March 8, 2024 and filed as Document 47 on March 18. Its remedy discussion states that a final judgment will vacate the 2023 replacement and its removal of the earlier text. The 2026 final rule independently confirms the resulting current regulatory action. This guide does not treat the district opinion as a complete current docket search or a ruling that a brand can never be an employer.

sections.heading: FLSA liability did not disappear with a reserved CFR part
paragraphs: Current FLSA Part 791 is reserved. DOL’s April 23, 2026 joint-employer publication is a proposed rule; its proposed factors and franchise examples must not be applied as an effective safe harbour. The source’s background distinguishes the 2020 FLSA rule, its rescission and litigation history from the NLRA framework. Actual governing FLSA court law and the employment facts still matter.

sections.heading: A real agency example: two businesses sharing a worker
paragraphs: DOL Opinion Letter FLSA2025-05 concerns a restaurant and members club with represented shared operations, managers and workers. On those stated facts, DOL concluded the worker’s hours had to be combined and both employers were responsible for FLSA compliance. The letter expressly limits itself to the supplied facts. Separate incorporation or payroll systems alone did not answer that actual agency inquiry; the letter is not a judgment about all network operators.

sections.heading: Output: a control and hours map
paragraphs: For each entity, record who actually selects workers, sets pay and individual schedules, supervises how work is done, disciplines and terminates. Keep ordinary brand/service standards and employment decisions in separate columns, including any mixed-purpose control. Add shared-worker hours and management evidence. Ask the NLRA, FLSA and relevant state questions separately; the franchise-definition analysis is another workstream.

practicalOutput: An entity/worker control-and-hours map with separate NLRA, FLSA and state questions.
limitations: No joint-employer finding, full circuit survey, bargaining-unit analysis or state-law clearance.
The 2026 FLSA proposal is not an effective franchise exemption or a substitute for current governing law.

title: Assign the consumer-product certificate and safety-reporting jobs
description: Check the actual product, responsible importer and 2026 eFiling phase before shipping branded equipment or stock.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Start with the product and intended use
paragraphs: The consumer-product definition and exclusions require an actual scope check. A B2B invoice, brand licence or equipment label does not decide the question. Identify the article, ordinary users, intended use, materials and other applicable agencies. This guide addresses the CPSC certificate/reporting pathway; it does not establish an electrical, machinery, food, pesticide or workplace standard for an unidentified product.

sections.heading: Certification and filing are assigned jobs
paragraphs: For covered imported finished products, Part 1110 defines the importer/certifier role, required certificate data and eFiling process. It allows specified broker/owner/purchaser/consignee allocations, but the identified certifier remains legally responsible for validity, accuracy, completeness and availability. Identify the applicable rules and actual testing basis; buying a certificate template is not compliance. The part also has five-year supporting-record requirements and conditions for access/furnishing.

sections.heading: Use the actual effective phase and policy distinction
paragraphs: The final rule makes its requirements effective July 8, 2026 for most covered products; specified FTZ entries have a January 8, 2027 phase. As of this review, the latter date is future. CPSC’s FAQ describes an initial policy of not seeking entry denial solely for missing eFiling data while continuing certificate enforcement. That enforcement description is not an exemption, a guaranteed entry outcome or permission to ignore applicable safety rules.

sections.heading: Keep a separate incident/reporting route
paragraphs: Under 15 USC § 2064(b), reasonably supported noncompliance, a potentially substantial product hazard or unreasonable serious-injury/death risk can trigger immediate reporting by the covered firms. Section 1115.14 interprets immediate as 24 hours, with its weekend/holiday computation, and warns against waiting for complete risk estimates. A reasonable investigation is not automatic permission to delay once reportable information is known. Name who receives complaints, preserves evidence and escalates promptly; a supplier’s promise to handle it does not answer every entity’s duty.

sections.heading: Output
paragraphs: Build a product/jurisdiction/standard/certifier matrix and a linked complaint-to-reporting workflow before distribution. Leave unverified standards, test exclusions, fees and authorisations unresolved. Obtain the actual product-specific evidence before dispatch and repeat the check when product, supplier, use or rule changes.

practicalOutput: A product-scope and certificate-responsibility matrix plus a complaint/reporting escalation workflow.
limitations: No particular product jurisdiction, standard/test result, approval, recall decision or shipment clearance.
CPSC import overview returned 403; current certification rule/final action/FAQ and actual statutes were readable and used instead.
eFiling enforcement language is time-sensitive and does not waive the underlying certificate or safety requirements.

title: Test the federal data-security gate before overseas access
description: Map actual data, volumes, people and agreements; an overseas support login can matter even without a file download.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Map access, not only transmission
paragraphs: Part 202 defines access broadly enough to include reading, viewing, editing or otherwise receiving data through systems and cloud platforms. The first screen is the actual U.S. person, foreign/covered person, data, volume and agreement. A remote support account may matter even if the database stays in the United States. Conversely, a foreign address alone does not establish a prohibited transaction.

sections.heading: Use the real data and party thresholds
paragraphs: The rule separates government-related data, which has specified regardless-of-volume criteria, from bulk U.S. sensitive personal data. Bulk aggregation uses the preceding 12 months and the specified same-party conditions, not a per-invoice reset. Exact category thresholds say more than 100 U.S. persons for human genomic data, more than 1,000 for other human-omic/biometric data, more than 1,000 U.S. devices for precise geolocation, more than 10,000 persons for health/financial data, and more than 100,000 persons for covered identifiers. Mixed datasets have their own rule. These counts alone are not a safe harbour for government-related data or other laws.

sections.heading: Do not substitute citizenship or an OFAC result
paragraphs: Part 202’s countries-of-concern and covered-person definitions include their own ownership, organisation, employment, primary-residence and designation rules. The current list names China, Cuba, Iran, North Korea, Russia and Venezuela; China has its stated Hong Kong/Macau definition. Citizenship alone is not the complete test. An OFAC name result is not the same determination, and an unlisted entity can still meet a defined category.

sections.heading: Separate prohibition, restriction and exemption
paragraphs: Data brokerage and specified human-omic transactions have prohibitions; relevant vendor, employment and investment transactions may be restricted subject to the actual security and other conditions. Corporate-group administrative/ancillary operations have a bounded exemption; an ordinary independent franchise/license partner is not assumed to be a qualifying subsidiary or affiliate. Restricted transactions require the current diligence program and annual audit conditions. Do not replace the prescribed security requirements with controls the business merely believes are equivalent.

sections.heading: Current dates and output
paragraphs: The program took effect April 8, 2025. The operative diligence/audit provisions refer to October 6, 2025; DOJ’s old good-faith enforcement-priority policy ran only through July 8, 2025 and is not continuing grace. Build a data/actor/access/agreement matrix, identify any supported exemption and assign unresolved technical controls and reporting. Keep customer/employee data in authorised systems outside this site.

practicalOutput: A federal DSP data/actor/access/agreement screen with explicit volumes, exemptions and unresolved controls.
limitations: No transaction authorisation, exemption finding, security attestation or complete privacy-law clearance.
CISA resource returned 403; detailed technical security requirements and their implementation remain unresolved.
DOJ overview says October 5 for a later phase; operative §§ 202.1001–1002 and its implementation policy say October 6. The guide follows those actual operative provisions.

title: Franchising or licensing: what changes the U.S. analysis?
description: Describe what your partner actually receives, pays and must do before choosing the legal workstream.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Start with the relationship, not its name
paragraphs: Calling an agreement a license does not settle whether the federal Franchise Rule applies. Section 436.1(h) asks about the brand, operating control or assistance, and required payment. A legal analysis must then consider exclusions, exemptions and independent state rules.

sections.heading: Prepare a relationship factsheet
paragraphs: For an established service company, the facts often sit in several places: the contract, onboarding presentation, software configuration, field-support promises and ordinary practice. Include indirect commitments to affiliates rather than listing only the headline royalty.
bullets: Who signs customer contracts and employs the delivery team?
Who licenses the brand, trains, recruits, sets service methods and monitors delivery?
What must the partner buy, pay or commit to pay, to whom, and when?
Where will the outlet operate, and where are offers made or received?

sections.heading: Fictional worked example: a technical-services license
paragraphs: A European maintenance brand proposes a license fee, branded vans, mandatory scheduling software, a training programme and required inspection methods. Those facts deserve a relationship review together. The software requirement alone does not decide the answer, and separating the fees into different invoices does not remove the need to examine them.

sections.heading: Who owns the next task?
paragraphs: The COO should document delivery controls; finance should map every payment; the expansion lead should map the parties and locations. The legal reviewer needs that evidence before designing a sales process. Record unresolved classification as unresolved, with a named person and next action. Completing the factsheet does not authorize an offer or sale.

practicalOutput: A relationship factsheet, payment map and list of classification questions.
limitations: This is a preparation guide, not a transaction-specific conclusion. State and local overlays remain separate.

title: When do training, software and standards become significant assistance?
description: Separate brand protection from the wider operating system your U.S. partner will rely on.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Assess the whole operating relationship
paragraphs: The FTC guide focuses on the overall method of operation and the partner’s reasonable reliance. It lists training, accounting systems, management advice and detailed operating manuals as examples to examine. Their existence is evidence, not an automatic classification result.

sections.heading: Keep a control inventory
paragraphs: For each requirement record its purpose, whether it is mandatory in practice, who can change it, how compliance is monitored and what happens if it is ignored. Distinguish trademark display or inspection solely protecting ownership rights from rules covering staffing, routes, pricing processes or customer restrictions.

sections.heading: Fictional worked example: facilities services
paragraphs: A logo guide tells an operator how to display the mark. A separate system dictates account acceptance, staffing levels, sales scripts, software, service reports and remedial visits. A reviewer needs both documents and actual support practice. Renaming the second document a quality appendix does not change its content.

sections.heading: The management output
paragraphs: The COO owns the inventory and should identify which elements are essential for consistent service. The team can then test a commercially workable model with its reviewer rather than deleting support indiscriminately to chase a label.
bullets: Record rights to exert control as well as controls already exercised.
Include pre-contract promises and routine assistance.
Leave the legal conclusion open until federal and state analyses are complete.

practicalOutput: An evidence-based control-and-assistance inventory.
limitations: This is a preparation guide, not a transaction-specific conclusion. State and local overlays remain separate.

title: What does the federal minimum-payment exemption actually count?
description: Map payments and commitments across the startup period; do not use an old figure as a universal franchise test.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Read the current exemption before restructuring payments
paragraphs: The current amount and precise window are held in the canonical rule record below. The rule looks at total required payments or commitments to the franchisor or an affiliate within its stated window. It is an exemption analysis after the relationship facts, not permission to ignore state law.

sections.heading: Count commitments, not only money already transferred
paragraphs: Finance should map initial fees, training, software, equipment, royalties and affiliate purchases where required by contract or practical necessity. The definition of required payment has an inventory exclusion for reasonable quantities bought at bona fide wholesale prices for resale or lease; it does not exclude every supply purchase.

sections.heading: Fictional worked example: the deferred invoice
paragraphs: A service brand delays collecting its fee but obtains an earlier commitment to pay it. Looking only at the bank statement misses the commitment. Record the contract date, due date, commencement date, recipient and business purpose before requesting the exemption analysis.

sections.heading: Keep the unresolved state work visible
paragraphs: A federal exemption does not resolve a state definition, business-opportunity law, dealer statute, advertising rule or relationship protection. The expansion lead should assign the relevant jurisdictions before any reliance decision. Do not show an unknown payment as zero.

practicalOutput: A dated payment-and-commitment schedule with an explicit state-review dependency.
limitations: This is a preparation guide, not a transaction-specific conclusion. State and local overlays remain separate.

title: Does one U.S. license avoid franchise obligations?
description: The single-trademark-license exclusion is narrow; licensees, outlets, future grants and state rules matter.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: One agreement is not the test
paragraphs: The FTC guide describes a narrow exclusion for a single licensee using a trademark. It does not establish a free first franchise, a free outlet or one license per state. A plan to create a network is a material fact to disclose to the reviewer.

sections.heading: Use the historical opinion carefully
paragraphs: FTC staff opinion 05-1, dated January 5, 2005, addressed a particular salon arrangement under an earlier rule citation. Staff expressly said the view was not binding on the Commission. Its footnote distinguishes the number of licensees from the number of outlets, and says intended future licenses would change the analysis.

sections.heading: Fictional worked example: three state agreements
paragraphs: A brand proposes one licensee in Texas, another in California and another in Illinois. Describing each as the sole license in its state does not make the overall plan a single-license arrangement. The team should preserve the complete rollout plan rather than reviewing each contract in isolation.

sections.heading: Prepare the complete grant history
paragraphs: The expansion lead should list existing and intended licensees, marks, goods or services, outlets, affiliates and termination rights. Ask separately whether state law recognizes any comparable treatment. Until those facts are reviewed, the planning status stays conditional.

practicalOutput: A trademark-grant register and a narrowly framed exclusion question.
limitations: This is a preparation guide, not a transaction-specific conclusion. State and local overlays remain separate.

title: Which locations matter before talking to a U.S. partner?
description: Build a transaction map before assuming that only the outlet state matters.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Map the offer and the parties
paragraphs: Federal disclosure and state sales requirements are separate layers.
